title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, and Comms Templates
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes Redwood Inference's standardized approach to on-call operations and incident response. It covers: incident severity definitions and lifecycle, runbook structure and examples, postmortem requirements and template, on-call rotations and escalation policies, annual game day guidance, and customer/ status page communications templates. The goal is to ensure consistent, fast, and blameless response that protects customer SLAs and preserves system reliability.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all engineering teams that own production services (Serving runtime, API, Dedicated, Private, Console, Observability). This document is the canonical source for incident handling procedures and comms templates.

Key contacts and ownership
-------------------------
- Incident Commander (IC): primary on-call for affected service
- Escalation lead: team tech lead for the service
- Communications lead: on-call or SRE on rotation for external comms
- Postmortem owner: IC (assigned within 48 hours)
- PagerDuty/Alert bindings: maintained in eng-sre/team-wiki

Incident severity matrix (S1	6	34)
--------------------------------
| Severity | Criteria (examples) | Customer impact | Target response time | IC responsibilities |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| S1 (Critical) | Service down, API errors > 30% or latency > 5x SLO | Major customer impact / outage | 5 minutes | Declare incident, page all hands, notify execs |
| S2 (High) | Significant degradation, e.g., increased latencies, partial feature outage | Moderate impact, degraded UX | 15 minutes | Triage, mitigation, escalate if not contained in 30 min |
| S3 (Medium) | Functional degradation in non-critical path, elevated error rates under threshold | Low customer impact | 60 minutes | Investigate during working hours, schedule fix |
| S4 (Low) | Informational, scheduled maintenance anomalies, low-severity regressions | No immediate customer impact | 24 hours | Log and plan remediation in next sprint |

Incident lifecycle (high-level)
-------------------------------
1. Detection & Triage
   - Alerts surface via monitoring, customer reports, or internal tests.
   - The on-call engineer acknowledges within target response time based on severity.
2. Declaration
   - If initial triage indicates S1 or S2, IC declares an incident in the incident channel (#incident-<service>), creates an incident Slack thread, and opens a War Room (Zoom/Meet).
3. Containment & Mitigation
   - Follow the runbook for the service. If no runbook exists, perform safe fallbacks (traffic diversion, scale up, rollback to last-known-good model/version).
4. Communications
   - Post status updates every 15 minutes for S1 until containment; every 30	60 minutes for S2. Use status page and customer templates (see templates below).
5. Resolution & Recovery
   - Validate fix, monitor for recurrence, and close the incident once stable for >30 minutes (S1/S2) or per agreed SLO window.
6. Postmortem & Follow-up
   - Draft a postmortem within 72 hours for S1/S2; within 7 days for S3 if customer-facing. Include timeline, root cause, remediation, and action owner/ETA.

Runbook structure (required fields)
----------------------------------
Every service runbook in Confluence must include the following flat sections (use this playbook as a template):
- Runbook title and service owner
- Pager/alert sources and symptom-to-severity mapping
- Quick triage checklist (what to check first)
- Known mitigations / commands to run (with safety notes)
- Escalation contacts (names, roles, Slack/phone)
- Post-incident cleanup steps
- Runbook test plan and last-tested date

Example quick triage checklist (Serving runtime)
------------------------------------------------
- Check the alerts dashboard: errors per minute, tail latency, GPU utilization.
- Confirm if deployment or model rollout happened in the last 30 min.
- Verify upstream dependencies (model store, auth, billing).
- Attempt a controlled request to a health endpoint (/healthz) and a minimal generation test.

Common mitigation commands (examples)
----------------------------------
- Scale up API replicas: kubectl scale deployment redwood-api --replicas=5
- Restart runtime service: systemctl restart redwood-runtime (on dedicated/private)
- Rollback to previous model: redwoodctl rollout rollback --service serving --revision vYYYYMMDD
- Drain node: kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data

Escalation policy
------------------
- Primary on-call (IC) for 15	6	30 minutes to resolve.
- If unresolved after 30 minutes, page secondary (team lead).
- If unresolved after 60 minutes or customer-impacting surge, page SRE escalation and product lead.
- Exec notification: S1 incident with >30 minutes unresolved or any incident with material customer or regulatory exposure.

On-call rotations & expectations
--------------------------------
- Rotation length: 1 week for engineering teams; 2 weeks for SRE.
- Handoff checklist: outstanding incidents, ongoing mitigations, paging thresholds changed, scheduled maintenance.
- Timezone coverage: Primary region is US-West; follow-the-sun rotations cover EU working hours by cross-team swap agreement.
- On-call compensation and support: see company-handbook/03_benefits-and-perks.

SLOs and alert thresholds (examples)
------------------------------------
- Serving API: p99 latency < 300ms (SLO), error rate < 0.1% (SLO).
- Alerts: page for 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m, or p95 latency > 1s sustained for 10m.

Postmortem template (required fields)
------------------------------------
- Title (incident id)
- Incident date/time (start/end)
- Severity
- Summary (one-paragraph)
- Timeline (timestamped events)
- Root cause analysis
- Immediate mitigations and resolution steps
- Impact (customers affected, pages, revenue/SLAs)
- Action items (owner, ETA)
- Follow-up verification (how to validate fix)
- Lessons learned and risk/controls to add

Postmortem process and timeline
-------------------------------
1. Draft initial postmortem within 72 hours (IC).
2. Review with stakeholders (SRE, product, legal if customer-impacting) within 7 days.
3. Publish final postmortem in Confluence and link to the incident ticket.
4. Track open action items in a dedicated engineering board and verify completion within 90 days.

Game days (exercise plan)
-------------------------
Purpose: validate runbooks, paging, and cross-team coordination. Recommended cadence: quarterly for critical services, biannual for non-critical.
Game day checklist:
- Pre-game: choose scenario, freeze deploys, notify stakeholders, schedule recording.
- During: execute scenario, follow runbook, time to acknowledge and containment metrics captured.
- Post-game: write a short report, capture gaps, create action items with owners and deadlines.

Status page and customer communications templates
------------------------------------------------
Use the platform status.redwood.ai for external updates; internal status templates live in this runbook. Keep external comms concise, factual, and avoid internal technical noise.

External status page template (S1 example)
Title: Service degradation impacting Redwood API (region US-West)
Impact: We are currently experiencing elevated error rates and increased latency for the Redwood API in the US-West region. Some requests may fail or experience significant delays.
Current status: Engineers have identified the root cause and implemented a mitigation; traffic is being routed to alternate capacity. We are monitoring performance.
Next update: in 15 minutes

Customer email template (short)
Subject: Incident affecting Redwood API (region and brief cause)
Hi {CustomerName},
We are currently investigating an issue affecting the Redwood API in {region}. Some requests may fail or be delayed. We've implemented a mitigation and are actively monitoring. We will provide an update by {time}.
If you have any immediate concerns, please reply to this email or contact support@redwood.ai.
Thanks,
Redwood Inference Operations

Customer escalation phone template (if needed)
Hi {CustomerName}, this is {ops_lead} from Redwood Inference. I'm calling to inform you we are aware of the issue affecting {service} in {region}. We have implemented a mitigation and are actively monitoring. Estimated time to resolution: {ETA}. We will keep you updated and connect you to our engineering lead for any technical questions.

Communications cadence guidance
- S1: external status updates every 15 minutes until resolution, internal updates every 5	6	15 minutes.
- S2: external updates every 30	6	60 minutes; internal every 15	6	30 minutes.
- S3	6	34: as needed; internal summary at incident close.

Runbook testing and maintenance
------------------------------
- Every runbook must be tested at least once per quarter (game day or smoke test).
- Record last-tested date in the runbook header.
- Major config or architectural changes require runbook review and owner sign-off before rollout.

KPIs and reporting
------------------
Track the following metrics monthly: mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), mean time to mitigate (MTTM), mean time to restore (MTTR), number of P1/P2 incidents, postmortem completion rate, and action-item closure rate. SRE team publishes monthly reliability report to eng-sre/dashboard.

Appendix: Incident ticket example (Jira fields)
- Summary: ServiceName outage - elevated errors (region)
- Priority: Critical
- Labels: incident, S1, service-name
- Reporter: oncall@redwood.ai
- Components: serving-runtime, api-gateway
- Linked pages: <link to Confluence postmortem>
